How to use this dashboard
Getting started

This dashboard contains a pre-built inventory of assets common for Canadian families in Ontario. Every asset is editable, and your changes are saved in your browser's local storage.

Switching look & feel

Use the Template dropdown in the header to switch between visual styles. Use the theme toggle to switch between light and dark mode.

Layout modes

The toolbar next to the logo lets you change how assets are displayed:

  • Dashboard — category cards with expandable sections
  • Table — sortable spreadsheet-like view with pagination
  • Kanban — assets grouped by status; drag cards between columns
  • Timeline — chronological view by open/purchase date
  • Detail — full field-by-field view of one asset
  • Compact — dense list grouped by category
  • Audit — traffic-light validation of every asset (missing values, beneficiary gaps)
  • Charts — pure-SVG allocation and liquidity charts (no libraries)
Finding assets

Use the search box to filter by asset name, institution, owner, or category. Use the Category and Owner dropdowns to narrow results, and click the status pills to show or hide assets by status.

Editing an asset

Click any asset card to open the edit panel; fields are grouped into sections. In the Table layout, double-click a cell to edit it inline, tick row checkboxes and use Bulk Edit to update many assets at once, and use ＋ Add Asset for a guided quick-add wizard. Changes are saved to your browser when you click Save Changes — or automatically when Auto-save is on.

Productivity tools

Kanban cards can be dragged between status columns. Use the Features menu for secondary views, appearance, file security and auto-save. Notes, alerts, and to-dos support Markdown.

File lock

The 🔒 button enables the file lock: the entire file is encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a passphrase derived from the owner's birth date (YYYYMMDD) plus a family word. The passphrase is never stored. When locked, opening the file in a browser prompts for the birth date and family word; a text editor only shows ciphertext. Several wrong attempts trigger a waiting period.

Exporting & saving

Save and Print stay visible in the header; use the Features menu for professional exports, import, appearance and security settings:

  • Export MD — download a Markdown summary of the filtered assets
  • Export Excel — download a CSV file compatible with Excel
  • Export JSON — download all assets as JSON for backup or import elsewhere
  • Import JSON — load a previously exported JSON file
  • Print — generate a print-ready estate binder
  • Save HTML — Chrome/Edge can save directly back to a bound inventory file; other browsers keep the staged Ctrl+S/download fallback
Keyboard shortcuts
  • Ctrl + S — save to browser storage
  • Ctrl + E — export Markdown
  • Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + Shift + Z — undo / redo
  • Esc — close any open panel
Privacy note

All edits are stored locally in your browser. No data is sent to any server. If you clear browser storage for this file, your edits will be lost, so use Save HTML to keep a permanent copy.
